summary: Completed Phase 1 (kernel), Phase 1.5 (sync), and Phase 2 (skills) in a single session. 76 files created, 168 tests passing. All 12 seed commands operational.
lessons: Bootstrap session needs kernel write protection temporarily disabled — use Python script to toggle, not sed
Sync pipeline should run BEFORE manual skill creation to avoid duplicate work
Seed commands should be created alongside the phases they serve, not deferred

summary: The sync tool preserves source directory paths (.agents/skills/) rather than remapping to target paths (skills/). This creates a dual-location issue where synced and hand-written skills live in different directories.
lessons: Sync tool needs a path_mapping config for source-to-target directory remapping
Architecture should decide: use source paths or Azoth paths as canonical

summary: Decided to hand-write all 8 core skills rather than extract via sync. The 5 'extracted' skills were authored from patterns observed in source framework commands, not directly copied. This produced cleaner, Azoth-native skills but bypassed the sync workflow.
lessons: Hand-writing produces better-adapted skills but is slower and doesn't validate the sync pipeline
Future skill additions should use sync-then-adapt workflow: extract via sync, then refine for Azoth conventions

goal: Deliver bootstrap PR and set up GitHub CLI
summary: gh CLI was not installed and Homebrew was absent. Installed gh directly via versioned zip to ~/.local/bin (already in PATH). This avoided sudo requirement entirely. PR created cleanly without co-authored-by in body.
lessons: Direct binary install to ~/.local/bin works when Homebrew/sudo unavailable — check PATH first before assuming package manager needed
Co-authored-by lines in PR bodies are unwanted — omit from gh pr create --body even when present in commits
